title: Interfaces
intro: Existing physical network interfaces and live engine interfaces appear automatically. Click a configured or engine interface to edit it; changes apply on Commit. Host-only interfaces are read-only.
addTitle: Add an interface to the configuration
addHelp: Engine interface name: host-<netdev> (af_packet lab interface), loop<N>, a NIC name or a bond. The agent creates host- and loop interfaces; other names must exist on the data plane.
addFailed: The interface could not be added to the candidate.
badName: Letters, digits, . _ / - ; starts with a letter
readonly: Your role can view but not change the configuration.

physical.releaseConfirm: Release {{name}} to the host? The engine will no longer use this NIC.
physical.reclaimConfirm: Reclaim {{name}} for the engine? The NIC will be used by the engine again.
physical.applyHint: This change is staged in the candidate and takes effect the next time the engine's start-up configuration is applied.
physical.builtInInfo: Built-in NIC ({{pci}}) used by the engine. You can edit or disable it, but not delete it — release it to the host instead.
physical.awaitingInfo: Built-in NIC ({{pci}}) waiting for the engine: its settings apply once the engine takes the NIC over.
physical.releasedInfo: NIC ({{pci}}) released to the host. Reclaim it to give it back to the engine.

drawer.label: Interface {{name}}
drawer.notInVpp: The engine has no interface with this name (yet). It appears after Commit if the agent creates it (host-, loop interfaces).
drawer.notConfigured: Not in the configuration: saving the form adds it to the candidate.
drawer.saved: Saved to the candidate. Commit to apply it.
drawer.subHint: A sub-interface is edited from its parent {{parent}}.
drawer.changedElsewhere: This interface changed in the candidate since you opened the form (another session). Only your own edits were saved; reload to see the combined result.

sub.title: Sub-interfaces (802.1Q)
sub.idHelp: Number after the dot in <parent>.<id>; usually the VLAN id
sub.idExists: Sub-interface {{id}} already exists: edit it from the table

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.help: admin state; interfaces stay down until enabled

mtu.title: MTU
mtu.help: L3 MTU in bytes (68–9216); empty = keep the driver default

mac.title: MAC address
mac.help: override the hardware address; empty = keep the burned-in MAC

promiscuous.title: Promiscuous
promiscuous.help: accept frames for any destination MAC

rxMode.title: RX mode
rxMode.help: polling (default for DPDK), interrupt or adaptive

vrf.title: VRF
vrf.help: routing table this interface belongs to

unnumbered.title: IP unnumbered
unnumbered.help: borrow the addresses of this interface (e.g. loop0); IPv4/IPv6 must then be empty

dhcpClient.title: DHCP client
dhcpClient.help: obtain an IPv4 address by DHCP; cannot be combined with unnumbered

innerVlanId.title: Inner VLAN ID
innerVlanId.help: inner tag for QinQ (not supported by this release)

dot1ad.title: 802.1ad outer tag
dot1ad.help: use an 802.1ad (0x88a8) outer tag instead of 802.1Q (0x8100)

inventory.title: Host network interface
inventory.readOnlyInfo: This physical interface was discovered automatically on the host. It is not configured in the engine; viewing it does not change its ownership or create configuration.
inventory.managementInfo: This interface carries host management traffic. Its discovered details are read-only; viewing it does not change management connectivity.
inventory.unavailable: {{source}} is unavailable. The list may be incomplete.
